note: Order of the guided run (/grammar/path) and of every topic list sorted by level (src/lib/lehrplan.js). This is a teaching decision, not a derived sort: within a level, what later topics build on comes first. Spanish order (2026-11-04, grammar-structure run): A1 starts with the subject pronouns, then gender, articles and plurals, then ser/estar and adjective agreement (which need gender), then the present (regular, key irregular, stem-changing) and the small everyday structures; A2 starts with reflexives, frequency and the two verb phrases that need no new forms (ir a, estar + gerund), then the three past tenses (perfecto, indefinido, imperfecto), then pronouns, verb + infinitive, comparison, quantity and place; B1 opens with the contrasts between the past tenses, then future, conditional and si, then the imperative as the door to the subjunctive (its negative forms are subjunctive forms), the subjunctive itself, and finally por/para, verbs + prepositions and the refinements; B2 starts with the imperfect subjunctive and unreal conditions, because the following subjunctive topics use them; C1 starts with the sequence of tenses and ends with formal style. Only topics listed here are part of the run (core). Topics left out are extra practice (reference and word-formation topics: wortarten, wortbildung-nomen): they keep their page and their place in the index, but they do not lengthen the run. Each topic must be listed under its own `level`. Drafts ("status": "entwurf") only count once they are reviewed. An entry "id:A2" would be the A2 part of a topic that teaches two levels on one page (exercise titles "A2: …"); no Spanish topic does this at the moment. `akkusativ` has its own page (/object-pronouns) and is named for the sorted lists, not as a run station. Keep GRAMMATIK_ORDER in src/lib/grammatikOrder.js in step.
